sc02_1.text: So what do you think the glasses are doing?
sc02_1.why: question: makes no claim; numbers and names are sourced

sc03_2.text: Your two eyes look from different but similar directions, so they see different images.
evidence: In binocular depth vision, the sensation arises from processing differences in retinal images resulting from the two eyes looking from different, but similar, directions.

sc03_3.text: And with an eye shut, I lose the other image?
sc03_3.why: question: makes no claim; numbers and names are sourced

sc03_4.text: Right. Your brain combines the two images, and you see a single 3D view with depth.
evidence: The two images are combined in the brain to give the perception of stereopsis; when viewed, the human brain perceives the images as a single 3D view, giving the viewer the perception of 3D depth.

sc04_2.text: Close. The projector puts both pictures on the same screen, each through a different filter.
evidence: To present stereoscopic images and films, two images are projected superimposed onto the same screen or displayed through different polarizing filters.

sc04_3.text: And each lens only lets its own picture through?
sc04_3.why: question: makes no claim; numbers and names are sourced

sc04_4.text: Exactly. The right eye's frames twist clockwise, the left eye's counter-clockwise, so each eye sees only its own frames.
evidence: A ZScreen circularly polarizes the frames clockwise for the right eye and counter-clockwise for the left eye; the audience wears circularly polarized glasses with oppositely polarized lenses so each eye sees only its designated frame.

sc05_1.text: Wait, so the pop-out effect is my own brain at work?
sc05_1.why: question: makes no claim; numbers and names are sourced

sc05_2.text: Yes! And that twist is circular polarization, so you can tilt your head without seeing double.
evidence: The advantage of circular polarization over linear polarization is that viewers are able to tilt their heads and look about the theater naturally without seeing double or darkened images.
